SketchLab: a study and revision guide

I built SketchLab to learn how probabilistic sketches (Theta and KLL) answer distinct-count and percentile questions on Databricks. This guide explains the project, the ideas behind it, the six steps I implemented, the app architecture, and the questions I should be able to answer about it.

Steps 1 to 6 executed by meSynthetic data onlyUnverified items are marked

How to use it: use the left panel to jump around, press Revision mode to hide long explanations, click any dotted term for a short definition, and use the copy button on any code block. Screenshots open larger when clicked.

Observed a number I saw in my own run. Concept general theory, not measured by me. Unverified a likely explanation I did not confirm. Not measured something I did not test.

  • Not measured Physical Delta storage saved. Sketch byte sizes alone do not prove storage savings.

AProject overview

The problem

Analytics teams often need two answers over many days of data: how many different visitors came, and what the 99th percentile response time was. Both are awkward at scale. Distinct counts cannot be added across days, because the same visitor appears on many days. Percentiles cannot be averaged across days, because each day has a different shape.

The idea

I store a small sketch for each day and campaign, then merge the sketches I need at query time. A merged sketch answers for the whole range without re-reading raw events.

raw_events400,000 rows
→
daily_sketches56 rows, one per day and campaign
→
Mergetheta_union_agg, kll_merge_agg_bigint
→
Compare with exactfrom raw_events
→
Streamlit appDatabricks Apps

Environment

  • Databricks Free Edition, serverless only. One 2X-Small SQL warehouse. One Databricks App.
  • Unity Catalog: catalog workspace, schema sketchlab.
  • Sketch functions in Databricks SQL (documented as available from Databricks Runtime and Databricks SQL 18.0). They come from Apache DataSketches.
  • Synthetic data. No real customer data.

Tables

TableColumnsRows
sketchlab.raw_eventsevent_date, visitor_id, campaign, page, response_time_ms (and others created in Step 1)400,000
sketchlab.daily_sketchesevent_date, campaign, event_count, theta_sketch (BINARY), kll_sketch (BINARY)56
One-sentence summary I can say in an interview

I stored mergeable Theta and KLL sketches per day and campaign in Delta tables, merged them with SQL to answer distinct-visitor and latency-percentile questions for any date range, validated the answers against exact queries, and served the comparison through a Streamlit app on Databricks Apps.

BFoundational concepts

Each concept follows the same pattern: what it is, why it matters, how it works, a simple example from my project, and the interview point. Click a card to focus on one concept.

Probabilistic data structures

What
A data structure that keeps a small summary of a large data set and gives approximate answers with a known kind of error.
Why
Exact answers need to keep or re-scan all the data. When data is large, that is slow or costly. A small summary can be good enough for many questions.
How
The structure uses hashing or sampling to decide what to keep. It has a size setting that trades accuracy for size. Theta and KLL are two such structures.
Example
For each day and campaign, I keep one Theta sketch (about 19,000 to 28,000 bytes in my data) as a BINARY value, instead of keeping a visitor list.
Interview
Approximate does not mean random or wrong. The error is bounded and tunable, but it is still an error. Always say which numbers are exact and which are estimates.

Approximate analytics

What
Answering analytics questions with estimates and a stated error, instead of exact values.
Why
Some questions (distinct count, percentile) are costly to answer exactly over many partitions, and exact partial results cannot be combined.
How
Keep a sketch per partition (here, per day and campaign). Merge the sketches you need. Read the estimate.
Example
Distinct visitors for Oct 3 to 9: exact 86,858, Theta estimate 85,225 in my run.
Interview
Use approximate analytics when the decision tolerates a small error and the question spans many partitions. Do not use it when exact audit numbers are required.

Theta sketch

What
A sketch that estimates the number of distinct items and supports union, intersection and difference.
Why
Counting distinct values exactly needs to remember every value seen. A Theta sketch remembers only a bounded number of hash values.
How
Each item is hashed to a number. The sketch keeps the smallest hashes up to a limit and a threshold. With many distinct items, the estimate is roughly (number kept) divided by (the threshold as a fraction of the hash range). With few distinct items, it keeps all of them and the count is exact.
Example
In Step 2, Campaign_D sketches matched the exact counts (2,807 and so on), while larger groups were slightly off.
Interview
Theta supports set operations, which a plain HyperLogLog-style count does not. The accuracy depends on the size setting (lgNomEntries in Databricks; the union default is 12).

KLL sketch

What
A sketch that estimates quantiles (percentiles) of a stream of numbers.
Why
Exact percentiles need sorting or holding all the values. KLL keeps a bounded sample.
How
It keeps items in levels. When a level fills, it is compacted: items are sorted and about half are kept, and each kept item then stands for more. Higher levels carry more weight. The size setting is k (merge default 200).
Example
Step 4 exact p99 was 2,192. KLL merged p99 gave 2,135 in one run and 2,654 in another.
Interview
KLL guarantees a small error in rank, not in value. In a thin tail, a tiny rank error can mean a big value difference.

Hashing and retained samples

What
A hash function turns an item into a number. The same item always gives the same number.
Why
This is what makes duplicates disappear. If V000042 appears on three days, it gives the same hash on all three days.
How
The Theta sketch keeps the smallest hash values it has seen. A duplicate hash is already in the kept set, so it adds nothing.
Example
Toy demo below: I keep the k smallest hashes and estimate the count from the k-th smallest.
Interview
Hashing spreads values evenly. That is why the smallest k hashes tell us how dense the whole set is.

Mergeability

What
Two sketches built on different data can be combined into one sketch that represents the combined data.
Why
This lets me precompute per day and combine only the days I need. I do not re-read raw events.
How
Theta: take the union of retained hashes and apply the lower threshold. KLL: combine the levels and compact as needed.
Example
theta_union_agg(theta_sketch) over 28 daily rows gave one merged sketch.
Interview
Mergeability is the reason sketches exist in a warehouse. A plain number like a distinct count is not mergeable.

Set union

What
The union of two sets contains every item that is in either set, once.
Why
Distinct count of days A and B is not count(A) + count(B). Visitors who came on both days are counted twice in the sum.
How
Theta union merges the hash sets, so shared visitors appear once.
Example
Sum of daily estimates: 184,667. Exact: 86,858. The sum was about 112.6% too high.
Interview
Distinct counts are not additive. This is the single most important idea in the project.

Percentile estimation

What
The p-th percentile is the value below which p percent of the data falls.
Why
Latency is usually described by p50, p90 and p99, because averages hide slow tails.
How
kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(sketch, 0.99) walks the weighted samples and returns the value at that rank.
Example
Exact p50, p90, p99: 151, 342, 2,192.
Interview
Percentiles cannot be averaged across days. The average of two daily p99 values is not the p99 of both days together.

Rank error vs value error

What
Rank error is how far the estimate's position is from the target position (in percentage points). Value error is the difference in the value itself (here, milliseconds).
Why
KLL controls rank error. In a sparse tail, values are far apart, so a small rank error becomes a large value error.
How
Count what fraction of raw rows are less than or equal to the estimate. Compare with the target.
Example
Estimate 2,654 for p99: value about 21% above exact, but rank 99.241%, about 0.24 points above 99.
Interview
When someone says your p99 is off by 20%, the right reply is to ask whether they mean value or rank.

Binary serialization

What
A sketch is turned into bytes so it can be stored in a column and read back later.
Why
Delta tables store ordinary column types. A BINARY column can hold the serialized sketch.
How
theta_sketch_agg and kll_sketch_agg_bigint return BINARY. The merge and estimate functions read that BINARY back into a sketch.
Example
daily_sketches has theta_sketch and kll_sketch as BINARY. length(theta_sketch) gives bytes (about 27,000 for large campaigns).
Interview
Only sketches made with the same library format can be merged. Do not mix a Theta binary with a KLL function.

Accuracy vs storage

What
Larger sketch settings keep more samples, so they are more accurate and bigger.
Why
This is the central trade-off. It is a design choice, not a free win.
How
Theta lgNomEntries and KLL k control size. I used the defaults and did not tune them.
Example
Merged Theta 25,618 B and merged KLL 4,676 B in my run.
Interview
Do not claim storage savings from sketch bytes alone. Delta stores files, and I did not measure them. Also, I did not tune any setting, so I make no claim about the best setting.

Demo 1: keep the smallest hashes (toy model)

This is a teaching toy, not the real DataSketches algorithm. Each item gets a random-looking number between 0 and 1. I keep only the k smallest numbers. If the set is big, the k-th smallest number tells me how crowded the set is.

Demo 2: sum versus union

Two days of visitors. Change the overlap and see why adding daily distinct counts goes wrong.

Demo 3: rank error becomes value error

I made 20,000 synthetic latencies with a heavy tail, like my project data. I shift the rank by a small amount and see how far the value moves.

CImplementation: Steps 1 to 6

Each step shows my real code, what it does, what I observed, and what the result does and does not prove. I removed the %sql line only in the explanation text. In a notebook SQL cell I keep it. In the SQL editor I remove it.

Step 1. Generate synthetic events

ExecutedPySpark notebook

Goal. Create 400,000 web events over 14 days with a shape that makes the sketches interesting: repeat visitors, uneven campaigns and pages, and a long tail of slow responses.

Where I ran it. A Databricks notebook (Python cell) on serverless compute.

Step 1: generate raw_events
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

SCHEMA = "sketchlab"
TABLE = f"{SCHEMA}.raw_events"

N_EVENTS = 400_000
N_VISITORS = 120_000
START_DATE = "2026-10-01"
N_DAYS = 14

spark.sql(f"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {SCHEMA}")

base = spark.range(1, N_EVENTS + 1).withColumnRenamed("id", "event_id")

events = (
    base
    # random date among 14 days
    .withColumn("event_date",
                F.date_add(F.lit(START_DATE).cast("date"),
                           F.floor(F.rand(1) * N_DAYS).cast("int")))
    # skewed visitor pool: rand^2 makes low IDs appear more often (repeat visitors)
    .withColumn("visitor_id",
                F.concat(F.lit("V"),
                         F.lpad((F.floor(F.pow(F.rand(2), F.lit(2.0)) * N_VISITORS) + 1)
                                .cast("string"), 6, "0")))
    # campaign with unequal traffic share
    .withColumn("_r", F.rand(3))
    .withColumn("campaign",
                F.when(F.col("_r") < 0.40, "Campaign_A")
                 .when(F.col("_r") < 0.70, "Campaign_B")
                 .when(F.col("_r") < 0.90, "Campaign_C")
                 .otherwise("Campaign_D"))
    # page chosen with skew
    .withColumn("_p", F.floor(F.pow(F.rand(4), F.lit(1.5)) * 6).cast("int"))
    .withColumn("page",
                F.element_at(F.array(F.lit("home"), F.lit("product"), F.lit("search"),
                                     F.lit("cart"), F.lit("checkout"), F.lit("support")),
                             F.col("_p") + 1))
    # latency in ms: log-normal body + ~2% slow tail, stored as BIGINT
    .withColumn("response_time_ms",
                (F.exp(F.lit(5.0) + F.lit(0.6) * F.randn(5))
                 + F.when(F.rand(6) < 0.02, F.rand(7) * 4000).otherwise(F.lit(0.0)))
                .cast("bigint") + 1)
    .drop("_r", "_p")
)

events.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(TABLE)

# ---- verification ----
spark.sql(f"""
SELECT COUNT(*)                         AS total_events,
       COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)       AS distinct_visitors,
       COUNT(DISTINCT event_date)       AS days,
       COUNT(DISTINCT campaign)         AS campaigns,
       COUNT(DISTINCT page)             AS pages,
       MIN(event_date)                  AS first_day,
       MAX(event_date)                  AS last_day,
       MIN(response_time_ms)            AS min_ms,
       MAX(response_time_ms)            AS max_ms
FROM {TABLE}
""").show(truncate=False)

spark.sql(f"SELECT campaign, COUNT(*) AS events FROM {TABLE} GROUP BY campaign ORDER BY campaign").show()
spark.sql(f"SELECT * FROM {TABLE} LIMIT 5").show(truncate=False)
spark.sql(f"DESCRIBE {TABLE}").show(truncate=False)

What the code does, in blocks

  • Constants. 400,000 events, 120,000 possible visitors, 14 days from 2026-10-01.
  • Seeds. rand(seed) with fixed seeds 1 to 7 makes the data repeatable.
  • visitor_id. pow(rand(), 2.0) pushes values toward 0, so low visitor numbers appear often. That creates repeat visitors, like real traffic.
  • campaign. One random number and thresholds 0.40, 0.70, 0.90 give campaign shares of 40, 30, 20 and 10 percent.
  • page. pow(rand(), 1.5) times 6 picks an index into six pages, with the first pages more common.
  • response_time_ms. exp(5.0 + 0.6 * randn()) is log-normal, so most values are a few hundred ms. About 2 percent of rows get extra random time up to 4,000 ms. That makes a heavy tail, which matters for p99.

Observed. Observed 400,000 events over 14 dates (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-14), four campaigns, six pages.

Proves. The data exists and has the shape I designed. Does not prove. Anything about real traffic.

Step 2. Build daily sketches

ExecutedDatabricks SQL

Goal. Turn raw events into one row per day and campaign, holding a Theta sketch of visitor_id and a KLL sketch of response_time_ms.

Step 2: build daily_sketches
%sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE sketchlab.daily_sketches AS
SELECT
  event_date,
  campaign,
  COUNT(*)                                  AS event_count,
  theta_sketch_agg(visitor_id)              AS theta_sketch,
  kll_sketch_agg_bigint(response_time_ms)   AS kll_sketch
FROM sketchlab.raw_events
GROUP BY event_date, campaign;

Then I checked a sample against exact values:

Step 2: spot-check sketches against exact counts
%sql
SELECT
  d.event_date,
  d.campaign,
  d.event_count,
  e.exact_visitors,
  theta_sketch_estimate(d.theta_sketch)             AS approx_visitors,
  kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(d.kll_sketch, 0.5) AS approx_p50,
  length(d.theta_sketch)                            AS theta_bytes,
  length(d.kll_sketch)                              AS kll_bytes
FROM sketchlab.daily_sketches d
JOIN (
  SELECT event_date, campaign, COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) AS exact_visitors
  FROM sketchlab.raw_events
  GROUP BY event_date, campaign
) e USING (event_date, campaign)
ORDER BY event_date, campaign
LIMIT 12;

What happens inside

  1. Spark reads raw_events and groups rows by (event_date, campaign). 14 days times 4 campaigns gives 56 groups.
  2. For each group, theta_sketch_agg hashes each visitor_id and keeps a bounded set of the smallest hashes. kll_sketch_agg_bigint keeps a bounded, compacted sample of response times.
  3. Each sketch is serialized into a BINARY value so it can sit in a Delta column.
  4. Delta writes Parquet files and a transaction log entry. The table is now 56 rows.

I use length() on a BINARY column to see the serialized size in bytes. That is the sketch size, not the Delta file size.

Observed. Observed 56 rows. In the 12 rows I checked, the estimates were close to the exact counts (for example Campaign_A on 2026-10-01: exact 10,315, estimate 10,178). For Campaign_D, the estimate equalled the exact count in every row I checked (2,807; 2,797; 2,780). Those sketches were also smaller (about 19,000 bytes against about 27,000). Concept A likely reason is that these groups had few enough distinct visitors for the sketch to keep every hash, but I did not test that.

Proves. Per-day sketches can be built in one SQL statement. Does not prove. That the estimates are accurate for every group. I only looked at 12 rows.

Step 3. Merge sketches over a date range

ExecutedDatabricks SQL

Goal. Answer for Oct 3 to Oct 9 by merging the stored sketches, and compare against the wrong shortcuts: adding daily distinct counts and averaging daily percentiles.

Step 3: merge and the wrong shortcuts
%sql
WITH m AS (
  SELECT
    theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)                                AS t,
    kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch)                             AS k,
    SUM(theta_sketch_estimate(theta_sketch))                     AS wrong_sum_of_daily_distinct,
    AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.5))         AS wrong_avg_of_daily_p50,
    AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.99))        AS wrong_avg_of_daily_p99,
    SUM(event_count)                                             AS raw_event_count
  FROM sketchlab.daily_sketches
  WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09'
)
SELECT
  wrong_sum_of_daily_distinct,
  theta_sketch_estimate(t)                  AS merged_distinct_visitors,
  ROUND(wrong_avg_of_daily_p50, 1)          AS wrong_avg_of_daily_p50,
  kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.5)    AS merged_p50,
  ROUND(wrong_avg_of_daily_p99, 1)          AS wrong_avg_of_daily_p99,
  kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.99)   AS merged_p99,
  kll_sketch_get_n_bigint(k)                AS merged_kll_item_count,
  raw_event_count
FROM m;

Why the query has two kinds of columns

  • theta_union_agg(theta_sketch) and kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch) are the correct way: they combine sketches.
  • SUM(theta_sketch_estimate(...)) and AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(...)) are the wrong shortcuts. I included them on purpose to see how wrong they are.
  • Everything is computed in a CTE called m, then the outer SELECT turns the merged sketches into numbers with the estimate functions.

Observed. Observed The range contains 28 daily sketch rows and 200,108 events. The wrong sum of daily distinct estimates was 184,667. The merged Theta estimate was 85,225.

Why the sum is wrong

A visitor who came on three days is counted three times in the sum. Merging removes duplicates because the same visitor produces the same hash.

Step 4. Exact baseline

ExecutedDatabricks SQL

Goal. Get ground truth from raw events for the same date range.

Step 4: exact answers
%sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                                                         AS raw_event_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)                                       AS exact_distinct_visitors,
  percentile_disc(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms)   AS exact_p50,
  percentile_disc(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms)   AS exact_p90,
  percentile_disc(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms)   AS exact_p99
FROM sketchlab.raw_events
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09';

Observed. Observed 200,108 events, 86,858 exact distinct visitors, exact p50 = 151, p90 = 342, p99 = 2,192.

Note on percentile_disc. It returns an actual value from the data (the discrete model) and its result type is DOUBLE. That is why the exact values look like 151.0 in a result grid.

Step 5. Compare approximate and exact

ExecutedDatabricks SQL

Goal. Put exact and approximate side by side, check sketch sizes, and test the percentile estimates by rank.

Step 5: comparison table
%sql
WITH a AS (
  SELECT theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)    AS t,
         kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch) AS k
  FROM sketchlab.daily_sketches
  WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09'
),
e AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)                                     AS d,
         percentile_disc(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p50,
         percentile_disc(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p90,
         percentile_disc(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p99
  FROM sketchlab.raw_events
  WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09'
),
r AS (
  SELECT 'distinct_visitors' AS metric, CAST(e.d AS DOUBLE) AS exact,
         CAST(theta_sketch_estimate(a.t) AS DOUBLE) AS approx FROM a, e
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'p50', e.p50, CAST(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(a.k, 0.50) AS DOUBLE) FROM a, e
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'p90', e.p90, CAST(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(a.k, 0.90) AS DOUBLE) FROM a, e
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'p99', e.p99, CAST(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(a.k, 0.99) AS DOUBLE) FROM a, e
)
SELECT metric, exact, approx,
       approx - exact                                  AS difference,
       ROUND((approx - exact) / exact * 100, 3)        AS pct_error
FROM r;

Observed. Observed

MetricExactApproximateError (derived)
Distinct visitors (Theta merged)86,85885,225about -1.88%
Sum of daily Theta estimates (wrong)86,858184,667about +112.6%
p99 (KLL merged), five separate runs2,1922,135 / 2,654 / 2,122 / 2,034 / 2,545about -2.6% / +21.1% / -3.2% / -7.2% / +16.1%

Error percentages are my own arithmetic from the observed values. The p99 values came from different runs of the query across steps and the app.

A mistake I made

I expected the Step 5 result to equal Step 3. It did not. KLL merged results changed between runs. I then added the rank check. Unverified My likely explanation is that KLL compaction uses randomness, or merge order matters. I did not confirm the cause. Theta results stayed the same across my runs.

Sketch sizes

Step 5: sketch byte sizes
%sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                                       AS daily_rows_used,
  SUM(length(theta_sketch))                      AS daily_theta_bytes_total,
  SUM(length(kll_sketch))                        AS daily_kll_bytes_total,
  length(theta_union_agg(theta_sketch))          AS merged_theta_bytes,
  length(kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch))       AS merged_kll_bytes
FROM sketchlab.daily_sketches
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09';
ItemBytes
28 daily Theta sketches, total711,349
28 daily KLL sketches, total108,244
Daily total (both)819,593
Merged Theta25,618
Merged KLL4,676
Merged total30,294

The merged pair is about 27 times smaller than the 28 daily pairs together (819,593 / 30,294). A merged Theta sketch is about the size of one daily Theta sketch (average daily Theta is about 25,405 bytes). Not measured Delta storage on disk. Not measured Speed.

Rank check

A percentile estimate can be judged by value or by rank. The rank check asks: what fraction of raw events are less than or equal to the value the sketch gave?

Step 5: rank check
%sql
SELECT v AS approx_value,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= v THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100, 3) AS exact_rank_pct
FROM sketchlab.raw_events
CROSS JOIN (SELECT explode(array(150, 344, 2135, 2654)) AS v)
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-10-03' AND '2026-10-09'
GROUP BY v
ORDER BY v;
Value testedExact rankTarget
15049.726%about p50
34490.166%about p90
2,13598.964%p99 estimate
2,65499.241%p99 estimate
What this shows

The p99 estimate of 2,654 looks 21% off by value, but it sits at rank 99.241%, only about 0.24 percentile points from the target. The 2,135 estimate sits at rank 98.964%, about 0.04 points away. In the sparse tail, a tiny rank gap becomes a large gap in milliseconds.

DDeep application architecture

This is what happens from the moment someone opens the app to the moment charts appear. Click any box, or step through the 12 steps.

Step 1 of 12

Click a box

Each box shows its job, what it does in SketchLab, and what can go wrong.

Authentication is not authorization

Authentication answers "who are you?". The app proves it is its own service principal using credentials the platform gives it. Authorization answers "what may you do?". Unity Catalog grants and the warehouse "Can use" permission decide that. The app can be authenticated and still be denied a table. These are two separate checks, and the guide keeps them separate.

Which identity is used here

My app queries as the app's service principal, not as the person using the app. So the grants must go to the service principal. A person who opens the app does not need table access, but they see whatever the app is allowed to read. Unverified Databricks also documents a user-authorization option for apps. I did not use it, and I have not verified its current behaviour or availability for Free Edition.

How the app starts

  1. Databricks Apps reads requirements.txt and installs the Python packages: databricks-sdk, databricks-sql-connector, streamlit, pandas.
  2. It reads app.yaml. The command field is the process to run: streamlit run app.py.
  3. The env section sets environment variables for that process. SKETCHLAB_CATALOG has a plain value (workspace).
  4. DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID uses valueFrom: sql-warehouse. That is a pointer to an app resource whose key is sql-warehouse. At start, the platform replaces the pointer with the real warehouse ID.
Why not hardcode the warehouse ID?

The code stays portable. If I attach another warehouse under the same key, I change no code. The resource also records the "Can use" permission for the app's identity, so the access is declared in one place.

Config termMeaning
commandThe process the platform starts
envList of environment variables for that process
valueFromRead the value from an attached app resource
resource key sql-warehouseThe name linking app.yaml to the resource I attached in the UI
os.getenv(...)Python reads an environment variable

The v2 code, block by block

Block 1: imports, constants, page setup, CSS

The top of the file imports Streamlit, pandas, Altair, the SQL connector and the SDK Config. The constants build the full table names from the catalog variable: workspace.sketchlab.raw_events and workspace.sketchlab.daily_sketches. They also set the allowed date range and the preset ranges. Next comes st.set_page_config and a CSS block that styles the hero, KPI cards and badges.

v2 block 1: imports, constants, page config, CSS

Line 25 of this block, cfg = Config(), creates the SDK configuration object that the connection code in Block 2 uses.

Block 2: connection and query helper

  • Config() comes from the Databricks SDK. It finds the host and credentials from the environment, which the platform sets for the app's service principal. Unverified I did not re-check which exact environment variables it reads today.
  • @st.cache_resource keeps one connection object for the whole app process. Streamlit reruns the script on every interaction, so without this, it would reconnect every time.
  • cfg.host includes https://. The connector wants a bare hostname, so the code removes the scheme. That value goes to server_hostname.
  • http_path is /sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>. It tells the connector which warehouse to send SQL to. The ID comes from os.getenv.
  • credentials_provider=lambda: cfg.authenticate hands the connector a way to get fresh authorization headers from the SDK config. The app identity is used here.
  • query() opens a cursor, runs cur.execute(), and gets the result as an Apache Arrow table with fetchall_arrow(). .to_pylist() turns it into a list of Python dictionaries, one per row.
v2 block 2: get_connection and query
@st.cache_resource
def get_connection():
    host = cfg.host.replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "")
    return sql.connect(
        server_hostname=host,
        http_path=f"/sql/1.0/warehouses/{os.getenv('DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID')}",
        credentials_provider=lambda: cfg.authenticate,
    )


def query(text):
    with get_connection().cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(text)
        return cur.fetchall_arrow().to_pylist()

Arrow. Apache Arrow is a column-based in-memory format. The connector can fetch results as Arrow and convert them cheaply. I used it because the result sets are small and the dictionaries are easy to read. .fetchall_arrow().to_pylist()[0] in v1 took only the first row, because those queries return one row.

Block 3: fetch, five queries, cached for 15 minutes

@st.cache_data(ttl=900) caches the returned results by the function's arguments for 900 seconds. That is different from cache_resource: cache_resource keeps a shared object (the connection) and cache_data keeps results (data that can be copied).

The where string is built with f-strings from dates and campaign names that come from fixed pickers. That is only safe because the user cannot type free text. If the app ever accepted free text, I would need query parameters instead.

Why two (or more) queries?

The approximate query reads only the small daily_sketches table. The exact query scans raw_events. They answer the same question from two different sources, so I can compare. The queries also use the same where filter, and the app checks that both read the same number of events (same_records).

v2 block 3: fetch
@st.cache_data(ttl=900, show_spinner=False)
def fetch(start_iso, end_iso, campaigns):
    # Dates and campaigns come from fixed pickers, so building this filter text is safe here.
    camps = ", ".join(f"'{c}'" for c in campaigns)
    where = f"event_date BETWEEN '{start_iso}' AND '{end_iso}' AND campaign IN ({camps})"

    approx = query(f"""
        WITH m AS (
          SELECT theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)    AS t,
                 kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch) AS k,
                 COUNT(*)                         AS sketch_rows,
                 SUM(event_count)                 AS events,
                 SUM(length(theta_sketch) + length(kll_sketch)) AS daily_bytes,
                 SUM(theta_sketch_estimate(theta_sketch))       AS naive_sum_distinct,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.50)) AS naive_p50,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.90)) AS naive_p90,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.99)) AS naive_p99
          FROM {DAILY} WHERE {where}
        )
        SELECT theta_sketch_estimate(t)                AS distinct_visitors,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.50) AS p50,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.90) AS p90,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.99) AS p99,
               length(t) AS merged_theta_bytes,
               length(k) AS merged_kll_bytes,
               sketch_rows, events, daily_bytes,
               naive_sum_distinct, naive_p50, naive_p90, naive_p99
        FROM m
    """)[0]
    if not approx["events"]:
        return None

    exact = query(f"""
        SELECT COUNT(*)                                                       AS events,
               COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)                                     AS distinct_visitors,
               percentile_disc(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p50,
               percentile_disc(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p90,
               percentile_disc(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p99
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where}
    """)[0]

    ranks = query(f"""
        SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p50'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r50,
               AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p90'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r90,
               AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p99'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r99
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where}
    """)[0]

    daily_approx = query(f"""
        SELECT event_date, theta_sketch_estimate(theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)) AS approx
        FROM {DAILY} WHERE {where} GROUP BY event_date ORDER BY event_date
    """)
    daily_exact = query(f"""
        SELECT event_date, COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) AS exact
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where} GROUP BY event_date ORDER BY event_date
    """)
    return approx, exact, ranks, daily_approx, daily_exact
  • Query 1 merges sketches and also computes the wrong shortcuts (naive sum and average).
  • Query 2 computes the exact values from raw events.
  • Query 3 is the rank check: it takes the sketch percentiles (int(approx['p50'])) and measures what fraction of raw events are less than or equal to each.
  • Queries 4 and 5 give per-day approximate and exact distinct counts for the day-by-day chart. In query 4, theta_union_agg groups by day, which merges campaigns within a day.
  • If the selection has no events, fetch returns None and the UI shows a warning instead of failing.

Block 4: helper functions

pct computes percent error. tone turns an error into a colour class (under 2% good, under 5% warn, otherwise bad). kpi builds the HTML for a card. These thresholds are my own display choices, not statistical standards.

v2 block 4: pct, tone, kpi
def pct(approx_value, exact_value):
    return (approx_value - exact_value) / exact_value * 100 if exact_value else 0.0


def tone(error_pct):
    size = abs(error_pct)
    return "good" if size < 2 else "warn" if size < 5 else "bad"


def kpi(label, value, sub="", badge=None, badge_tone="good"):
    tag = f'<span class="badge {badge_tone}">{badge}</span> ' if badge else ""
    return (f'<div class="kpi"><div class="lbl">{label}</div><div class="val">{value}</div>'
            f'<div class="sub">{tag}{sub}</div></div>')

Block 5: sidebar controls

Streamlit widgets (selectbox, date_input, multiselect, button) return their current value. Every change reruns the whole script top to bottom. The guards handle bad input: a custom date range with only one date, or no campaign selected, shows a message and calls st.stop(), which ends the run cleanly. The Re-run button clears the data cache and reruns.

v2 block 5: sidebar
# ---------------- sidebar ----------------
st.sidebar.header("Controls")
preset = st.sidebar.selectbox("Date range", list(PRESETS.keys()))
if PRESETS[preset] is None:
    picked = st.sidebar.date_input("Pick start and end", value=(date(2026, 10, 3), date(2026, 10, 9)),
                                   min_value=MIN_DAY, max_value=MAX_DAY)
    if len(picked) != 2:
        st.sidebar.info("Pick both a start date and an end date.")
        st.stop()
    start, end = picked
else:
    start, end = PRESETS[preset]
campaigns = st.sidebar.multiselect("Campaigns", CAMPAIGNS, default=CAMPAIGNS)
if not campaigns:
    st.sidebar.warning("Select at least one campaign.")
    st.stop()

st.sidebar.divider()
if st.sidebar.button("Re-run queries"):
    st.cache_data.clear()
    st.rerun()
st.sidebar.caption("Results are cached for 15 minutes. Re-run to rebuild the merged sketches. "
                   "KLL percentiles can change slightly between runs.")
st.sidebar.divider()
st.sidebar.caption("Data: 400,000 synthetic website events, 14 days, 4 campaigns, 6 pages.")

Block 6: hero, data fetch, KPI cards

The hero is HTML written with st.markdown(..., unsafe_allow_html=True). The spinner wraps fetch. Note that tuple(campaigns) is passed because cache arguments must be hashable. Then the code converts results to numbers and builds the four KPI cards in st.columns(4).

v2 block 6: hero, fetch, KPI cards
# ---------------- hero ----------------
st.markdown(
    '<div class="hero"><h1>SketchLab</h1>'
    "<p>Approximate answers from tiny stored sketches, checked against exact answers from the raw events.</p>"
    '<span class="pill">Theta sketch</span><span class="pill">KLL sketch</span>'
    '<span class="pill">Delta tables</span><span class="pill">Synthetic data</span></div>',
    unsafe_allow_html=True,
)
st.caption(f"Selection: {start:%b %d} to {end:%b %d}  |  {', '.join(campaigns)}")

with st.spinner("Querying the SQL warehouse..."):
    result = fetch(start.isoformat(), end.isoformat(), tuple(campaigns))
if result is None:
    st.warning("No data for this selection.")
    st.stop()
approx, exact, ranks, daily_approx, daily_exact = result

d_exact = float(exact["distinct_visitors"])
d_approx = float(approx["distinct_visitors"])
d_err = pct(d_approx, d_exact)
same_records = int(approx["events"]) == int(exact["events"])
merged_bytes = int(approx["merged_theta_bytes"]) + int(approx["merged_kll_bytes"])
daily_bytes = int(approx["daily_bytes"])
sketch_rows = int(approx["sketch_rows"])

k1, k2, k3, k4 = st.columns(4)
k1.markdown(kpi("Exact distinct visitors", f"{int(d_exact):,}", "counted from raw events"), unsafe_allow_html=True)
k2.markdown(kpi("Sketch estimate (Theta)", f"{int(round(d_approx)):,}", "vs exact",
                f"{d_err:+.2f}%", tone(d_err)), unsafe_allow_html=True)
k3.markdown(kpi("Events in selection", f"{int(exact['events']):,}",
                "same records in both" if same_records else "records do NOT match",
                "match" if same_records else "check", "good" if same_records else "bad"),
            unsafe_allow_html=True)
k4.markdown(kpi("Merged sketch size", f"{merged_bytes:,} B",
                f"from {sketch_rows} daily sketches ({daily_bytes:,} B)"), unsafe_allow_html=True)
st.write("")

Blocks 7 to 11: charts, tables and tabs

These blocks build a pandas DataFrame of exact and approximate percentiles, then draw them in four tabs. I show them for completeness.

Block 7: latency DataFrame
v2 block 7
latency = []
for name in ["p50", "p90", "p99"]:
    e, a = float(exact[name]), float(approx[name])
    latency.append({"metric": name, "exact_ms": e, "sketch_ms": a, "difference_ms": a - e,
                    "error_pct": round(pct(a, e), 3)})
lat = pd.DataFrame(latency)

tab1, tab2, tab3, tab4 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Why merging works", "Sketch size", "How it works"])
Block 8: Overview tab (percentile chart, error chart, table, rank check, CSV download)
v2 block 8
# ---------------- tab 1: overview ----------------
with tab1:
    left, right = st.columns(2)
    with left:
        st.subheader("Latency percentiles")
        long = lat.melt(id_vars="metric", value_vars=["exact_ms", "sketch_ms"], var_name="kind", value_name="ms")
        long["kind"] = long["kind"].map({"exact_ms": "Exact", "sketch_ms": "Sketch"})
        chart = (
            alt.Chart(long)
            .mark_bar(cornerRadiusEnd=5)
            .encode(
                x=alt.X("kind:N", title=None, axis=None),
                y=alt.Y("ms:Q", scale=alt.Scale(type="log"), title="milliseconds (log scale)"),
                color=alt.Color("kind:N", scale=alt.Scale(domain=["Exact", "Sketch"], range=[SLATE, INDIGO]),
                                title=None),
                column=alt.Column("metric:N", title=None, header=alt.Header(labelOrient="bottom")),
                tooltip=["metric", "kind", alt.Tooltip("ms:Q", format=",.0f")],
            )
            .properties(width=110, height=260)
        )
        st.altair_chart(chart)
    with right:
        st.subheader("Observed error")
        err = pd.DataFrame({
            "metric": ["distinct visitors", "p50", "p90", "p99"],
            "error_pct": [d_err] + list(lat["error_pct"]),
        })
        err["direction"] = err["error_pct"].apply(lambda v: "below exact" if v < 0 else "above exact")
        bars = (
            alt.Chart(err)
            .mark_bar(cornerRadiusEnd=6)
            .encode(
                x=alt.X("metric:N", sort=None, title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
                y=alt.Y("error_pct:Q", title="error vs exact (%)"),
                color=alt.Color("direction:N",
                                scale=alt.Scale(domain=["below exact", "above exact"], range=[INDIGO, CYAN]),
                                legend=None),
                tooltip=["metric", alt.Tooltip("error_pct:Q", format="+.3f")],
            )
            .properties(height=260)
        )
        zero = alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y": [0]})).mark_rule(color="gray").encode(y="y:Q")
        st.altair_chart(bars + zero, use_container_width=True)

    st.dataframe(lat, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

    st.subheader("Rank check")
    st.markdown(
        '<div class="note">A KLL sketch aims to be accurate in <b>rank</b>: how far along the sorted data a value sits. '
        "A small rank gap can still be a big gap in milliseconds when the data is sparse, like the slow tail.</div>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )
    r1, r2, r3 = st.columns(3)
    for col, (name, target, key) in zip([r1, r2, r3], [("p50", 50, "r50"), ("p90", 90, "r90"), ("p99", 99, "r99")]):
        rank = float(ranks[key]) * 100
        col.markdown(
            kpi(f"Sketch {name} = {int(approx[name]):,} ms", f"{rank:.2f}%",
                f"of real events are at or below it (target {target}%)",
                f"{rank - target:+.2f} pts", "good" if abs(rank - target) < 1 else "warn"),
            unsafe_allow_html=True,
        )
    st.write("")
    summary = pd.concat([
        pd.DataFrame([{"metric": "distinct_visitors", "exact": d_exact, "sketch": d_approx,
                       "difference": d_approx - d_exact, "error_pct": round(d_err, 3)}]),
        lat.rename(columns={"exact_ms": "exact", "sketch_ms": "sketch", "difference_ms": "difference"}),
    ])
    st.download_button("Download results (CSV)", summary.to_csv(index=False), "sketchlab_results.csv", "text/csv")

The CSV button is st.download_button with the CSV text built from a DataFrame. Streamlit gives the browser a file to download.

Block 9: Why merging works tab
v2 block 9
# ---------------- tab 2: why merging works ----------------
with tab2:
    st.subheader("Unique visitors: three ways to answer")
    naive_sum = float(approx["naive_sum_distinct"])
    cmp_df = pd.DataFrame({
        "method": ["Exact count", "Merged Theta sketch", "Add up daily estimates"],
        "visitors": [d_exact, d_approx, naive_sum],
    })
    base = alt.Chart(cmp_df).encode(
        y=alt.Y("method:N", sort=None, title=None),
        x=alt.X("visitors:Q", title="distinct visitors"),
    )
    bars = base.mark_bar(cornerRadiusEnd=6).encode(
        color=alt.Color("method:N", scale=alt.Scale(domain=list(cmp_df["method"]), range=[SLATE, INDIGO, RED]),
                        legend=None),
        tooltip=["method", alt.Tooltip("visitors:Q", format=",.0f")],
    )
    labels = base.mark_text(align="left", dx=5).encode(text=alt.Text("visitors:Q", format=",.0f"),
                                                       color=alt.value("#9ca3af"))
    st.altair_chart((bars + labels).properties(height=190), use_container_width=True)
    over = pct(naive_sum, d_exact)
    st.markdown(
        f'<div class="note">Adding up the stored daily estimates gives <b>{int(naive_sum):,}</b>, which is '
        f"<b>{over:+.1f}%</b> away from the exact count. The same visitor is counted again for every day and "
        "campaign they appear in. Merging the Theta sketches is a set union, so each visitor counts once.</div>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )

    st.subheader("Day by day")
    dd = pd.DataFrame(daily_exact).merge(pd.DataFrame(daily_approx), on="event_date")
    dd["day"] = pd.to_datetime(dd["event_date"]).dt.strftime("%b %d")
    day_long = dd.melt(id_vars="day", value_vars=["exact", "approx"], var_name="kind", value_name="visitors")
    day_long["kind"] = day_long["kind"].map({"exact": "Exact", "approx": "Sketch"})
    line = (
        alt.Chart(day_long)
        .mark_line(point=True)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("day:N", sort=list(dd["day"]), title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
            y=alt.Y("visitors:Q", title="distinct visitors per day"),
            color=alt.Color("kind:N", scale=alt.Scale(domain=["Exact", "Sketch"], range=[SLATE, INDIGO]), title=None),
            tooltip=["day", "kind", alt.Tooltip("visitors:Q", format=",.0f")],
        )
        .properties(height=260)
    )
    st.altair_chart(line, use_container_width=True)
    st.markdown(
        f'<div class="note">If you add the exact daily distinct counts above you get <b>{int(dd["exact"].sum()):,}</b>, '
        f"but the true distinct count for the whole range is <b>{int(d_exact):,}</b>. Even exact daily numbers "
        "cannot be added.</div>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )

    st.subheader("Percentiles: merging vs averaging")
    pr = []
    for name in ["p50", "p90", "p99"]:
        e, m, n = float(exact[name]), float(approx[name]), float(approx[f"naive_{name}"])
        pr.append({"metric": name, "exact": e, "merged sketch": m, "average of daily p-values": round(n, 1),
                   "merged error %": round(pct(m, e), 3), "averaged error %": round(pct(n, e), 3)})
    st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(pr), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
    st.caption("Averaging ignores how many events each group holds. In this synthetic data every day follows the "
               "same pattern, so averaging can look fine or even closer. That is a property of this dataset, not "
               "a reason to trust it.")

        "the single merged sketch. I have not measured the raw table's size, so this does not claim a saving "
        "against the raw events. Sketch size depends on the sketch settings and the data.</div>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )

# ---------------- tab 4: how it works ----------------
with tab4:
    with st.expander("What is a sketch?", expanded=True):
        st.markdown(
            "A sketch is a small, specially designed summary stored as binary. It does not keep a readable list of "
            "your records. It keeps just enough to estimate one kind of answer, and compatible sketches can be merged."
        )
    with st.expander("Theta sketch: counting distinct visitors"):
        st.markdown(
            "Each visitor ID is turned into a number (a hash). The sketch keeps only the smallest hashes. "
            "A repeat visitor gives the same hash, so it is stored once. The count is estimated from how many "
            "hashes are kept. With few distinct values nothing is dropped, so the answer can be exact. "
            "This is the general DataSketches idea."
        )
    with st.expander("KLL sketch: percentiles"):
        st.markdown(
            "A KLL sketch keeps sorted sample values with weights. Percentiles are read by walking the samples "
            "and adding up their weights. Its accuracy promise is about rank, so in a sparse tail the millisecond "
            "value can move more."
        )
    with st.expander("Why can't I add daily counts or average daily percentiles?"):
        st.markdown(
            "A daily distinct count has lost the information about who the visitors were, so overlapping visitors "
            "get counted again. A percentile depends on the whole distribution and on how many events each group "
            "holds, so averaging percentiles is generally not the percentile of the combined data."
        )
    with st.expander("When should I use exact calculations?"):
        st.markdown(
            "Whenever the number must be exact, for example finance, billing or compliance evidence. "
            "Sketches suit decision-support questions where a small error is acceptable."
        )

st.caption("Synthetic data. Results come from this dataset and are not general guarantees. "
           "Query speed is not measured here. Badge colours use simple display thresholds "
           "(under 2% green, under 5% amber) that I chose for readability.")

Complete v2 app.py
import os
from datetime import date

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from databricks import sql
from databricks.sdk.core import Config

CATALOG = os.getenv("SKETCHLAB_CATALOG", "workspace")
RAW = f"{CATALOG}.sketchlab.raw_events"
DAILY = f"{CATALOG}.sketchlab.daily_sketches"
CAMPAIGNS = ["Campaign_A", "Campaign_B", "Campaign_C", "Campaign_D"]
MIN_DAY, MAX_DAY = date(2026, 10, 1), date(2026, 10, 14)
PRESETS = {
    "Oct 3 - 9 (my test range)": (date(2026, 10, 3), date(2026, 10, 9)),
    "Week 1 (Oct 1 - 7)": (date(2026, 10, 1), date(2026, 10, 7)),
    "Week 2 (Oct 8 - 14)": (date(2026, 10, 8), date(2026, 10, 14)),
    "Full dataset (Oct 1 - 14)": (MIN_DAY, MAX_DAY),
    "Single day (Oct 5)": (date(2026, 10, 5), date(2026, 10, 5)),
    "Custom range": None,
}
INDIGO, CYAN, SLATE, RED = "#6366f1", "#06b6d4", "#94a3b8", "#ef4444"

cfg = Config()

st.set_page_config(page_title="SketchLab", page_icon="🧪", layout="wide")

st.markdown(
    """
<style>
.block-container {padding-top: 1.4rem; max-width: 1300px;}
.hero {background: linear-gradient(120deg,#4f46e5 0%,#7c3aed 50%,#06b6d4 100%);
       border-radius: 18px; padding: 26px 32px; margin-bottom: 14px; color: #ffffff;}
.hero h1 {margin: 0; font-size: 2.1rem; color: #ffffff; padding: 0;}
.hero p {margin: 6px 0 0 0; opacity: .93; font-size: 1.02rem; color: #ffffff;}
.pill {display: inline-block; padding: 3px 11px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: .78rem;
       background: rgba(255,255,255,.2); margin: 12px 6px 0 0; color: #ffffff;}
.kpi {border: 1px solid rgba(128,128,128,.28); background: rgba(128,128,128,.07);
      border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px 18px; height: 100%;}
.kpi .lbl {font-size: .76rem; opacity: .7; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .05em;}
.kpi .val {font-size: 1.85rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1.25; margin-top: 4px;}
.kpi .sub {font-size: .84rem; opacity: .8; margin-top: 4px;}
.badge {display: inline-block; padding: 2px 9px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 600;}
.good {background: rgba(16,185,129,.18); color: #10b981;}
.warn {background: rgba(245,158,11,.18); color: #f59e0b;}
.bad {background: rgba(239,68,68,.18); color: #ef4444;}
.note {border-left: 4px solid #6366f1; padding: 8px 14px; background: rgba(99,102,241,.08);
       border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0; font-size: .92rem; margin: 6px 0 10px 0;}
</style>
""",
    unsafe_allow_html=True,
)


@st.cache_resource
def get_connection():
    host = cfg.host.replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "")
    return sql.connect(
        server_hostname=host,
        http_path=f"/sql/1.0/warehouses/{os.getenv('DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID')}",
        credentials_provider=lambda: cfg.authenticate,
    )


def query(text):
    with get_connection().cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(text)
        return cur.fetchall_arrow().to_pylist()


@st.cache_data(ttl=900, show_spinner=False)
def fetch(start_iso, end_iso, campaigns):
    # Dates and campaigns come from fixed pickers, so building this filter text is safe here.
    camps = ", ".join(f"'{c}'" for c in campaigns)
    where = f"event_date BETWEEN '{start_iso}' AND '{end_iso}' AND campaign IN ({camps})"

    approx = query(f"""
        WITH m AS (
          SELECT theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)    AS t,
                 kll_merge_agg_bigint(kll_sketch) AS k,
                 COUNT(*)                         AS sketch_rows,
                 SUM(event_count)                 AS events,
                 SUM(length(theta_sketch) + length(kll_sketch)) AS daily_bytes,
                 SUM(theta_sketch_estimate(theta_sketch))       AS naive_sum_distinct,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.50)) AS naive_p50,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.90)) AS naive_p90,
                 AVG(kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(kll_sketch, 0.99)) AS naive_p99
          FROM {DAILY} WHERE {where}
        )
        SELECT theta_sketch_estimate(t)                AS distinct_visitors,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.50) AS p50,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.90) AS p90,
               kll_sketch_get_quantile_bigint(k, 0.99) AS p99,
               length(t) AS merged_theta_bytes,
               length(k) AS merged_kll_bytes,
               sketch_rows, events, daily_bytes,
               naive_sum_distinct, naive_p50, naive_p90, naive_p99
        FROM m
    """)[0]
    if not approx["events"]:
        return None

    exact = query(f"""
        SELECT COUNT(*)                                                       AS events,
               COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)                                     AS distinct_visitors,
               percentile_disc(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p50,
               percentile_disc(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p90,
               percentile_disc(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY response_time_ms) AS p99
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where}
    """)[0]

    ranks = query(f"""
        SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p50'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r50,
               AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p90'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r90,
               AVG(CASE WHEN response_time_ms <= {int(approx['p99'])} THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS r99
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where}
    """)[0]

    daily_approx = query(f"""
        SELECT event_date, theta_sketch_estimate(theta_union_agg(theta_sketch)) AS approx
        FROM {DAILY} WHERE {where} GROUP BY event_date ORDER BY event_date
    """)
    daily_exact = query(f"""
        SELECT event_date, COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) AS exact
        FROM {RAW} WHERE {where} GROUP BY event_date ORDER BY event_date
    """)
    return approx, exact, ranks, daily_approx, daily_exact


def pct(approx_value, exact_value):
    return (approx_value - exact_value) / exact_value * 100 if exact_value else 0.0


def tone(error_pct):
    size = abs(error_pct)
    return "good" if size < 2 else "warn" if size < 5 else "bad"


def kpi(label, value, sub="", badge=None, badge_tone="good"):
    tag = f'<span class="badge {badge_tone}">{badge}</span> ' if badge else ""
    return (f'<div class="kpi"><div class="lbl">{label}</div><div class="val">{value}</div>'
            f'<div class="sub">{tag}{sub}</div></div>')


# ---------------- sidebar ----------------
st.sidebar.header("Controls")
preset = st.sidebar.selectbox("Date range", list(PRESETS.keys()))
if PRESETS[preset] is None:
    picked = st.sidebar.date_input("Pick start and end", value=(date(2026, 10, 3), date(2026, 10, 9)),

For comparison: v1 connection code

v1 used the same connection pattern with a simpler run() helper that returns the first row only.

v1: get_connection, run, pct
@st.cache_resource
def get_connection():
    host = cfg.host.replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "")
    return sql.connect(
        server_hostname=host,
        http_path=f"/sql/1.0/warehouses/{os.getenv('DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID')}",
        credentials_provider=lambda: cfg.authenticate,
    )


def run(query):
    with get_connection().cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(query)
        return cur.fetchall_arrow().to_pylist()[0]


def pct(approx, exact):
    return (approx - exact) / exact * 100 if exact else 0.0

Request lifecycle for one click

  1. I change the date preset. The browser tells Streamlit over its connection.
  2. Streamlit reruns app.py from line 1.
  3. get_connection() returns the cached connection.
  4. fetch(...) is called. If the arguments match a result less than 900 seconds old, the cached value is returned and no SQL runs.
  5. Otherwise, five SQL statements go to the warehouse. Unity Catalog checks the service principal's privileges on each table.
  6. Results come back, the script builds DataFrames, and Streamlit sends updated elements to the browser.
Not verified by me

Where exactly the Apps reverse proxy and its sign-in sit, and how long the warehouse takes to start when idle, are platform details. I describe them only in general terms. I did not measure warehouse start time.

LayerWhat controls itIn SketchLab
Who is the app?App service principal (created automatically with the app)Identity used by Config()
Can it use the warehouse?Warehouse permission "Can use", granted through the app resourceResource key sql-warehouse
Can it see the catalog and schema?USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMAOn workspace and workspace.sketchlab
Can it read the tables?SELECT on each tableraw_events, daily_sketches
  • Least privilege. I granted only SELECT. The app cannot change data.
  • No secrets in code. The warehouse ID comes from a resource. The client ID and secret that belong to the service principal are provided to the app environment by the platform and are not in my code or in this guide.
  • SQL injection. The f-string filters are safe only because inputs come from fixed widgets. Free text would need parameterized queries.
  • Data. All data is synthetic. In a real project, a raw_events grant would be a bigger decision than a daily_sketches grant.
  • Guide hygiene. I cropped or hid screenshots that showed personal identifiers.
Do users need table access?

With the service principal model, the people using the app do not need table grants. They see what the app shows. That is convenient, but it also means the app, not Unity Catalog, decides who sees what. Unverified Whether I should add app-level sharing rules is a decision I have not made.

FTroubleshooting

My deployment worked, so I report no deployment errors. Only two cases below happened to me or were made on purpose. All others are scenarios I prepared and I label them as hypothetical. The fixes are reasoned from the code and documented behaviour, not from tests.

1. The app does not start
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
Deployment fails or the app shows an error page right after start.
Likely reason
The command in app.yaml is wrong, or app.py has a syntax error, or requirements.txt has a bad package name.
Diagnose
Open the app logs in the Apps UI and look at the first error.
Smallest fix
Correct the line named in the log. For example, the command must be ['streamlit', 'run', 'app.py'].
Verify
Redeploy and wait for the status to become running.
2. ModuleNotFoundError for a package
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The log says a module such as databricks.sql cannot be found.
Likely reason
The package is missing from requirements.txt. The PyPI name is databricks-sql-connector, but the import is from databricks import sql.
Diagnose
Compare each import in app.py with a line in requirements.txt.
Smallest fix
Add the missing package name to requirements.txt.
Verify
Redeploy and check that the log shows no import error.
3. DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID is None
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
Queries fail and the path contains the text None.
Likely reason
The SQL warehouse resource is not attached, or its key does not match the valueFrom name in app.yaml.
Diagnose
Check the app's resources. The key must be exactly sql-warehouse. Then print os.getenv('DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID') once in a test.
Smallest fix
Attach the warehouse resource with that key, or fix the key name in app.yaml.
Verify
Redeploy. The http_path should end with a real warehouse ID.
4. Invalid http_path or cannot connect to the warehouse
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The connector raises an error while opening the connection.
Likely reason
The path is malformed (for example a None ID), or the server_hostname still contains https://.
Diagnose
Check that server_hostname has no scheme and http_path is /sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>.
Smallest fix
Keep the host-cleaning code in get_connection and the env var wiring from the resource.
Verify
A simple SELECT 1 through query() returns a row.
5. Permission denied or table not found
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
A query fails with a permission error or says the table or view cannot be found.
Likely reason
The app service principal lacks USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA or SELECT. Missing privileges can show up as not found in some cases.
Diagnose
Run SHOW GRANTS on the schema and tables, and check the principal name carefully (it is easy to grant to the wrong one).
Smallest fix
Re-run the three GRANT statements for the app's service principal.
Verify
Reload the app. The queries return rows.
6. First query is slow or times out
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The first page load after a pause is much slower than later ones.
Likely reason
The SQL warehouse may be stopped and needs to start. I did not measure start time.
Diagnose
Look at the warehouse state in the SQL Warehouses page.
Smallest fix
Wait for the warehouse to start, then reload. The spinner in the app covers this.
Verify
Later loads are fast, or use cached data for 15 minutes.
7. Authentication fails
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The connection returns an authorization or invalid token error.
Likely reason
Credentials in the app environment are missing or invalid, or Config() is not finding them.
Diagnose
Check the app logs, and confirm the app has an assigned service principal.
Smallest fix
Redeploy the app so that the platform injects the credentials again. Check the documentation for the variables Config() reads.
Verify
get_connection() succeeds and a test query runs.
8. Empty result for the selection
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The app says no data for this selection.
Likely reason
The chosen dates are outside 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-14, or the campaign list is empty.
Diagnose
Check the selection line under the hero.
Smallest fix
The app already returns None from fetch() and shows a warning. Pick a valid range.
Verify
The KPI cards appear.
9. Sketch function not found
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
An error like 'function theta_sketch_agg cannot be found'.
Likely reason
The compute does not support the DataSketches functions. They are documented from Databricks Runtime and Databricks SQL 18.0.
Diagnose
Check the runtime or warehouse version.
Smallest fix
Use compute that supports these functions.
Verify
SELECT theta_sketch_estimate(theta_sketch_agg(...)) runs.
10. Merged distinct count is far too high
Demonstrated on purpose
What happened
The distinct count over a range is about double the exact value.
Likely reason
Daily distinct estimates were added. Visitors who appear on several days were counted several times.
Diagnose
Compare with theta_union_agg and with an exact COUNT(DISTINCT).
Smallest fix
Merge with theta_union_agg, then estimate once.
Verify
Merged estimate 85,225 against exact 86,858 (Step 3 and Step 4). I created the wrong sum on purpose in Step 3, so this one was a demonstration, not an accident.
11. KLL percentile changes between runs
Actually experienced
What happened
p99 gave 2,135, then 2,654, 2,122, 2,034 and 2,545 for the same range.
Likely reason
Hypothesis only: KLL compaction involves randomness, or merge order affects the result. I did not confirm the cause.
Diagnose
Re-run the query several times. Then run the rank check.
Smallest fix
No fix is needed for a valid estimate. Judge by rank, not by value. A larger k would reduce error, but I did not test that.
Verify
Rank check: 2,135 is at 98.964%, and 2,654 at 99.241%.
12. App shows old numbers after changing data
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
I changed the tables but the app still shows earlier results.
Likely reason
fetch() is cached for 900 seconds with st.cache_data.
Diagnose
Compare the app with a direct SQL query.
Smallest fix
Press Re-run queries in the sidebar, which clears the data cache.
Verify
The numbers match the SQL result.
13. App stops by itself
Hypothetical, I did not hit this
What happened
The app was working yesterday, and now it is stopped.
Likely reason
Databricks documents that Free Edition apps stop after 24 hours. I did not observe this directly.
Diagnose
Check the app status in Compute, then Apps.
Smallest fix
Start the app again.
Verify
Status shows running and the page loads.

GFinal app walkthrough (v2)

These are screenshots from my deployed v2 app. I explain what each shows and which numbers come from where.

Sidebar and overview

The sidebar holds the date presets, campaign picker and the Re-run button. The note under it says results are cached for 15 minutes and that KLL percentiles can change slightly between runs.

The KPI cards compare exact distinct visitors with the Theta estimate and show a badge for the error. The percentile chart uses a log scale so p50 and p99 can share a chart. The error bars show percent difference per metric.

Why merging works

The wrong sum is much larger than the exact value, because repeat visitors are counted once per day.

Each day alone, the sketch is close to exact. The problem only appears when I add days.

Rank check

This tells me the percentile estimate by rank. In my v2 run, the values 152, 340 and 2,545 had exact ranks of 50.60%, 89.87% and 99.17%. That confirms the rank error is small even when the p99 value is far from 2,192.

Sketch size

The tab shows serialized sketch bytes for the daily sketches and for the merged sketches. This is a comparison of serialized sketch sizes only. It is not a claim about Delta file size on disk or about speed.

How it works and CSV export

The Overview tab has a Download results (CSV) button. It exports the summary table. I did not capture a screenshot of the downloaded file, so I show no CSV content here.

HInterview and revision questions

Try to answer each question out loud before opening it.

BeginnerWhat is a sketch?

A small summary of a column that can answer some questions approximately and can be merged with other sketches. In my project it is a BINARY value in a Delta table.

BeginnerWhat does Theta answer and what does KLL answer?

Theta answers distinct counts and set operations. KLL answers percentiles.

BeginnerWhat is approximate analytics?

Using a small summary to get an estimate instead of scanning all the data. I accept a small error to get a small, mergeable summary.

BeginnerWhy did I generate synthetic data?

To have repeatable data with repeat visitors and a heavy latency tail, without using real data. The seeds are fixed.

BeginnerWhat is a Delta table and why store sketches in one?

Delta is a table format with a transaction log on top of Parquet files. A sketch is a BINARY column, so I can store it like any other column.

BeginnerWhat does GROUP BY event_date, campaign do in Step 2?

It makes one group per day and campaign. With 14 days and 4 campaigns, I got 56 groups and 56 rows.

BeginnerWhy does the app need a SQL warehouse?

The app has no Spark of its own. It sends SQL through the SQL connector and a warehouse runs the SQL.

BeginnerWhat does length() on a sketch return?

The size of the serialized sketch in bytes. It is not the size on disk.

IntermediateWhy can I not add daily distinct counts?

Because the same visitor can appear on several days. A sum counts that visitor once per day. In my data the sum was 184,667 against an exact 86,858.

IntermediateWhy can I not average daily percentiles?

A percentile depends on the whole distribution. The average of two daily p99 values is not the p99 of the combined days. I averaged them in Step 3 only to show the wrong approach.

IntermediateWhy does merging Theta sketches remove duplicates?

The same visitor ID hashes to the same value. The union keeps one copy of that hash.

IntermediateHow does a Theta sketch estimate the count?

It keeps the smallest hash values up to a limit. With many distinct items, the density of those smallest hashes tells the size of the whole set. I explain this in simple terms only. With few distinct values, it keeps every hash and the answer is exact, as I saw for Campaign_D.

IntermediateWhat is the difference between theta_union_agg and theta_union?

theta_union_agg is an aggregate function that merges many sketches in a group, one per row. theta_union combines two sketches given as arguments.

IntermediateWhy use percentile_disc for the exact value?

It returns an actual value from the data (the discrete model) and is the closest match to what a sketch returns. A continuous percentile can interpolate between values, so it could return a number that is not in the data. Its result type is DOUBLE.

IntermediateWhy does the app run two or more queries?

One reads the small sketch table (approximate), one scans raw events (exact), so I can compare. Extra queries give the rank check and the per-day chart.

IntermediateWhat is the difference between st.cache_resource and st.cache_data?

cache_resource keeps one shared object, here the connection. cache_data stores returned data, here the query results, and I set ttl=900 so they expire after 15 minutes.

IntermediateWhy does Streamlit rerun the script on every click?

That is its execution model. Every widget interaction reruns app.py from the top. Caching and st.stop() make that manageable.

IntermediateWhat does valueFrom: sql-warehouse do?

It tells the platform to fill the environment variable from the app resource whose key is sql-warehouse. The code never contains the real warehouse ID.

IntermediateWhat does Config() do?

It is the Databricks SDK configuration object. It finds the host and credentials from the environment. The connector then asks it for authorization headers through cfg.authenticate.

IntermediateWhy strip https:// from the host?

server_hostname expects a bare host name, and cfg.host includes the scheme.

IntermediateWhat does fetchall_arrow().to_pylist() do?

fetchall_arrow returns the result as an Apache Arrow table. to_pylist turns that into a list of Python dictionaries, one per row.

IntermediateWhat are the three grants the app needs?

USE CATALOG on the catalog, USE SCHEMA on the schema, and SELECT on each table. They go to the app's service principal.

IntermediateWhat happens if the selection has no data?

fetch() returns None when the event count is zero, and the page shows a warning and stops cleanly.

IntermediateHow do I know the sketch and the exact query used the same records?

Both queries use the same where filter. The app compares the event count from the sketch table (SUM of event_count) with the exact COUNT(*) and shows a match badge.

TrickyIs the app authenticated, or is it authorized?

Both, and they are separate. It is authenticated as its service principal. It is authorized only for what the grants and the warehouse permission allow.

TrickyWhose permissions does the query use?

In my implementation, the app's service principal, not the person viewing the app. So grants go to the service principal. I did not use user authorization, and I have not verified its current behaviour.

TrickyWhy did my p99 jump from 2,135 to 2,654 while Theta did not move?

I observed that. My unconfirmed explanation is that KLL has randomness in compaction or depends on merge order. The rank check showed both values are close to the target rank. I did not test the cause.

TrickyThe p99 estimate is 21% off. Is the sketch wrong?

Not necessarily. KLL bounds rank error, not value error. The estimate 2,654 had an exact rank of 99.241%, about 0.24 points from the target. In the sparse tail, small rank gaps become big value gaps.

TrickyThe merged sketches are 27 times smaller. Did I save 27 times the storage?

No. That compares serialized sketch bytes only. I did not measure Delta storage on disk, and I would still keep the daily sketches. It is a size comparison for the sketches, not a storage-saving claim.

TrickyDoes the sketch make the query faster?

I did not measure speed, so I make no claim. The sketch query reads 28 small rows instead of 200,108 events, but that is a reason to test, not a result.

TrickyIs building SQL with f-strings in the app a security problem?

It can be. In my app the date and campaign values come from fixed widgets, so the user cannot type free text. With free text input, I would need parameterized queries.

TrickyWhy does the app use theta_union_agg on a per-day GROUP BY in query 4?

Each day has up to four campaign sketches. Merging them gives the day's distinct visitors across campaigns, which I then compare with the exact count for that day.

TrickyWhich numbers in this guide are guarantees?

None. They are observations from one synthetic dataset. The general behaviour (mergeability, rank error) is documented theory, but my error percentages are not guarantees.

TrickyHow would I make the p99 more stable?

A larger k for KLL should reduce error, but I did not test it. I would also run the query several times and compare ranks. I mark that as an idea, not a result.

TrickyWhy not hardcode the warehouse ID?

A hardcoded ID breaks when the warehouse changes, and it hides the access dependency. With a resource, the platform supplies the ID and records the permission.

TrickyWhat is the difference between @st.cache_resource on get_connection and a normal global variable?

Streamlit reruns the script, so a plain global would be recreated each time. cache_resource keeps the object across reruns and sessions.

TrickyWhat would break if I gave USE SCHEMA but not USE CATALOG?

The service principal could not reach the schema, because access needs the whole path: catalog, schema, then table. The queries would fail.

TrickyWhy can a smaller group have an exactly correct Theta estimate?

With few distinct values, the sketch can keep every hash, so it counts them directly. I saw this for Campaign_D (estimate equal to exact). I inferred the reason from theory and did not test it.

IQuick revision cheat sheet

One-page summary

Raw events become one Theta sketch and one KLL sketch per day and campaign, stored as BINARY in daily_sketches. For a range, theta_union_agg and kll_merge_agg_bigint merge the stored sketches and the estimate functions read the answer. Exact answers come from raw_events. My results: Theta was about 1.9% low on distinct visitors, KLL p99 moved between runs but stayed close by rank, and the merged sketches were about 27 times smaller than the 28 daily ones. A Streamlit app on Databricks Apps queries as its service principal through a SQL warehouse.

Key results (one dataset)

  • 400,000 events, 14 days, 56 daily sketch rows
  • Oct 3 to 9: 28 rows, 200,108 events
  • Exact distinct 86,858; Theta merged 85,225 (about -1.88%)
  • Sum of daily estimates 184,667 (about +112.6%)
  • Exact p50 / p90 / p99 = 151 / 342 / 2,192
  • KLL p99 across runs: 2,135; 2,654; 2,122; 2,034; 2,545
  • Merged sketches 30,294 B vs daily 819,593 B (about 27x)

Five common mistakes

  1. Adding daily distinct counts across days.
  2. Averaging daily percentiles.
  3. Judging a tail percentile only by value, not by rank.
  4. Claiming storage or speed savings from sketch bytes alone.
  5. Giving table grants to a user when the app runs as its service principal.

Ten things I must remember

  1. Sketches are approximate and mergeable.
  2. Theta answers distinct counts and set operations.
  3. KLL answers percentiles and has rank error.
  4. Distinct counts cannot be summed; percentiles cannot be averaged.
  5. Merging works because the same item gives the same hash.
  6. BINARY columns store serialized sketches; length() gives bytes.
  7. KLL results can vary between runs; Theta was stable in my runs.
  8. The app runs as a service principal; grants go to it.
  9. Authentication and authorization are different checks.
  10. Results come from one synthetic dataset, not a guarantee.

Sources and evidence

  • My own work: the notebook and SQL code, screenshots and written notes in my project PDF. These are the source of every observed number here.
  • Documentation to re-check when behaviour matters: the Databricks documentation at docs.databricks.com (Databricks SQL function reference for the theta and kll functions, Databricks Apps, Unity Catalog, SQL warehouses, Free Edition limits) and Apache DataSketches at datasketches.apache.org. I checked the function names and the 18.0 availability earlier while building. I did not re-open these pages while writing this guide.
